html:
SMTO-WEB-0006 — SMTO couldn't get an answer from the search service

GUID: dea9e6f1-e1e5-4c29-8156-8977f641c389
Slug: web-provider-unavailable
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web

What happened

  • SMTO tried to send your web search to the search service set up for it, but couldn't connect or got an error back instead of results. No search results came back.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you use your own search server (for example SearXNG), make sure it is switched on and running, and that the computer running SMTO can reach it over the network. SMTO tried every address for that server and none accepted the connection, or the server answered with an error.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Capabilities, select Configure Web, check the provider's Base URL, then select Test connection. The test sends one small search and shows the exact problem for that provider.
  3. To keep searching meanwhile, choose another enabled provider as Default provider, or set Fallback search to Also when the default provider fails, then select Save. SMTO can then use a provider that is reachable.

What success looks like

  • Test connection shows Connected, and a new web search in a conversation returns results.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the search server or your network. Don't turn off secure connection checks or the private-address protection to make the server reachable.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Web search provider could not be used: it returned a non-success HTTP status other than the classified 401/403/406 cases, or no validated address accepted a connection.

What this means

  • Search receives another non-success HTTP status, or connection attempts exhaust validated addresses without a usable connection. The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.

Why this can happen

  • Search receives another non-success HTTP status, or connection attempts exhaust validated addresses without a usable connection.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the recorded status or connection exception to distinguish provider failure from transport failure.

How to fix it

  • Check the recorded status_code and message for the provider attempt; in src/agent_runtime/skills/web/transport.py open_get.connect tries each resolved address under the provider's timeout_seconds deadline and raises when none connect. Verify the provider process, base_url, DNS, firewall and TLS certificate from the Server host, then run Test connection; keep TLS verification and private-address checks enabled.
  • Verify the configured Web provider, network and service health.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberate bounded read reaches the configured service and receives valid results.

What not to do

  • Do not disable TLS or private-address protection to make a provider reachable.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
